clues.text: After Lot reached Zoar, the LORD rained down sulfur and fire from heaven on this city and its neighbor.
The LORD told Abraham that the outcry against this city was great and its sin very grievous.
The morning after its fall, Abraham looked down toward it and saw smoke rising like smoke from a furnace.
In Abram's day, Birsha was king of this city when four kings led by Chedorlaomer made war on it.
As this city's king fled from battle in the Valley of Siddim, some men fell into its tar pits.
Jesus said this city would find the day of judgment more bearable than a town that rejected His disciples.
A prophet warned that the Ammonites, who taunted Israel, would become like this city, a place of weeds and salt pits.
